All 20 backend pytest tests pass (auth cookie+bearer, profile, sessions, upload with real AI quality, analyze with real gpt-5.6-terra metrics + non-diagnostic summary, timeline, progress, /api/files auth, export, delete). minor.issue: AI quality prompt is very strict — most stock hair photos (portraits) fail unless they clearly show scalp. The AI's quality<60 rejection is by design but users may hit it repeatedly with normal selfies; consider softening the prompt or lowering the threshold.

integration_issues.issue: Every visit to /upload calls POST /api/sessions unconditionally in useEffect. That creates a new empty tracking_session (visible on Timeline as an un-analyzed week) each time the user opens the page — clicking around cluttered our timeline with Week 2 'Not analyzed'. Consider creating the session lazily on first successful upload, or reusing an existing empty session.

action_items: Optional UX: make Upload.jsx lazy-create the tracking_session on first successful upload instead of on component mount, or reuse the most recent empty session, to avoid cluttering the timeline with empty weeks.
Optional: consider clarifying / softening the AI quality prompt so ordinary user selfies with visible hair (not just top-of-head scalp shots) aren't rejected with quality<20.
Delete AlertDialog confirmation flow was not clicked in this run (destructive); backend DELETE /api/account itself is verified via pytest test_20.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_current_user helper handles both cookie and Bearer, and normalizes tz-aware/naive expires_at strings — good.

server.py Line 210 `upload_image` accepts Header(None) via param but the actual auth is read from request.cookies OR authorization header inside get_current_user — fine. Note: `authorization` param is fetched via default None (not Header()) since it's declared as plain Optional[str] — FastAPI treats it as query param. In practice tests still worked via cookie/Bearer through get_current_user (which reads from request directly). Verify Bearer header reaches server via `request.headers.get('authorization')` instead of relying on this param. (This bug is silent because get_current_user re-reads the header, but the endpoint signatures are misleading.) Actually server.py reads `authorization: Optional[str] = Header(None)` in most endpoints, but in `upload_image` (line 210) it's `authorization: Optional[str] = Header(None)` — OK. Verified passing bearer works.

ai_service.py: default fallbacks in exception paths return quality=72 and neutral scores (65/68/70/75). This masks provider failures — a broken key would still 'succeed' with hardcoded 65/68/70. Consider raising 502 when the AI call fails so the UI can distinguish real AI output from silent fallback.
Upload.jsx creates a new session on every mount (useEffect with []) → clutters timeline. See integration_issues.
storage.py get_object retries after a 404 by re-initing the storage key — good pattern; but init_storage() is not concurrency-safe (module-level `storage_key`). Not a bug for single-worker uvicorn.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Dashboard, Timeline, Upload, Settings, Results, dark mode toggle, upload+analyze, ProtectedRoute redirect)

test_credentials: Seeded per iteration via mongosh/pymongo as per /app/memory/test_credentials.md. No app passwords.
seed_data_creation: conftest.py fixture seeds `users` + `user_sessions` with a UUID/timestamp-based session_token (7d expiry). Test fixture image at /app/backend/tests/fixtures/scalp_front.jpg (74KB portrait, scored 82 at 'front' view). Cleanup runs on session teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests are in single class TestReHairEndToEnd with numbered methods (test_01..test_20) so xdist loadscope keeps them on one worker and class attrs (session_id, storage_path, uploaded) flow between tests. Use /app/backend/tests/fixtures/scalp_front.jpg with view='front' — it reliably scores >60 with the AI quality check; top/left/right synthetic images are rejected. Real gpt-5.6-terra calls happen in ~2-3s each (visible in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log LiteLLM lines).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no blocking bugs. Timeline shows 'not analyzed' entries because Upload.jsx auto-creates sessions on page mount (see integration_issues.upload-page).
